messages:
ashley: Heads-up — nightly perf dashboard just alerted a sustained throughput dip starting ~00:15 UTC: ~28% lower p50 throughput for short sequences (<=64). :rotating_light:
ben: saw that. any correlation with the midnight merge?
carla: which metric exactly? can you paste the chart?
ashley: pasted small screenshot to thread (link) — it's the per-shard throughput heatmap, spike in latency and drop in tokens/sec for small payloads. also saw KV eviction rate jump.
dmitri: ci-bot posted a failed perf run earlier, think it was the merge that landed kernel-selector adjustments + batching tweak.
ci-bot: nightly-perf-run #2024 failed: 4.3% regression in short-seq throughput, bench suite run id=perf-2024-04-18-00. Logs: https://ci.internal/perf/2024-04-18/2024.
eva: quick triage idea — kernel selector epsilon was relaxed in the merge, could cause less-optimal kernel picks for short sequences and more frequently trigger prefetch paths.
ben: also the batching window reduction change could increase scheduler churn for small requests. they landed both in the same PR.
carla: can someone run a targeted perf reproduce locally? simple loadgen for seq=32, batch size histogram.
dmitri: running now: run: ./perf/loadgen --seq=32 --qps=300 --duration=600s --capture-batches. will attach results.
ben: thanks. also grab KV cache metrics: hit rate, evictions/s, avg keep-time.
dmitri: attached: batch_histogram.txt + kv_metrics.json + flame.svg. initial glance: batching distribution shifted — more 1-2 request batches, less steady 8-12 batching we usually see.
ashley: flame shows more time in kernel_prober(choose) and kernel_context_switch.
eva: kernel_prober heavier implies selector executing more heuristics per request. maybe the epsilon change increased probe attempts.
carla: KV metrics: eviction_rate x3, hotset churn high. suggests we are promoting different keys into cache perhaps due to altered batching order.
ben: that matches: smaller batches mean different interleaving and less KV reuse across the batch, may cause more misses and worse throughput.
dmitri: micro profile of selector in CPU shows branch mispreds up ~40% in choose_kernel().
ashley: interesting. could be a fast-path that used to be taken but now misses and falls back to slower path.
eva: do we have the PR diff? which file changed?
ben: PR 4832 — selector: relax_epsilon -> from 0.03 to 0.07; batching: prefer_low_latency flag enabled by default.
carla: propose revert of prefer_low_latency (it's the risky one) until we can tune selector interactions. anyone object?
ashley: +1 for revert as hotfix, but let's not do both reverts. revert prefer_low_latency first.
dmitri: I've prepared a revert branch, will run CI perf smoke before proposing.
ci-bot: running perf-smoke on revert/4832-revert-lowlat... status: queued.
eva: while CI runs, can we simulate with synthetic traffic that mirrors small-req pattern (seq<=64, high qps, low concurrency)? we need to confirm KV hit rate improvement if revert applied.
ben: yes I have a loadgen script to emulate heavy small-req workloads. running it now with baseline (main at commit X) vs. candidate (revert branch).
dmitri: baseline run: p50 tokens/sec 1250, candidate run: p50 tokens/sec 1680 — that’s +34% in local reproduce. KV hit rate improves from 68% -> 87%.
ashley: that's promising. any regressions in large-seq cases?
dmitri: quick check: seq=512 throughput no change within noise.
carla: CI-perf-smoke passed on revert candidate with short-seq benchmarks green. ci-bot: perf-smoke passed.
ci-bot: nightly-perf is still failing on main; revert branch shows no regression.
ben: recommend emergency revert today, create follow-up issue to re-evaluate selector epsilon and batching interplay with KV.
eva: agree. we'll need A/B rollout plan for revert and monitor nightdash for next 24h.
ashley: filing rollout ticket and will tag ops for a short maintenance window to apply revert to canary then prod if stable.
carla: add dashboards to track: small-seq p50/p95 tokens/sec, KV hit rate, batch size histogram, selector probe count.
dmitri: logging PR+revert links: PR4832 (landed), PR4840 (revert prefer_low_latency).
ben: follow-up: let's also add an integration test that simulates small-req KV locality so we catch this before landing future batching changes.
ashley: agreed. thanks everyone for fast triage. keeping thread open until canary finishes ramp. :thumbsup:
ben: updating incident postmortem draft now.
ci-bot: canary rollout of revert scheduled at 2325020000 UTC.
eva: canary metrics look good at +1hr.
ashley: closing triage — will publish short blameless postmortem when rollout fully validated.
carla: noted lessons: avoid coupling kernel_selector epsilon and batching defaults in single PR. create smaller, isolated rollouts.
dmitri: saved attach: batch_histogram_before_after.png and perf_diff_table.csv.
ashley: thanks all. moving to follow-up tasks.
